repairReply.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color deck built around bending triggers that draw cards and chain into creature loops. Allies, Lessons, and Shrines fill the graveyard and battlefield while earthbending, waterbending, firebending, and airbending each pull a card. The deck can assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander to loop creature enter and leave triggers for unlimited tokens and storm count.

strategy.text: Ramp early with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to cast the commander around turn 3.
Cast Lesson spells and bending abilities to trigger [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]]'s card draw.
Build toward four bending types in one turn to transform into [[Aang, Master of Elements]] for a burst of value.
Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] for infinite loops.
Use Allies and Shrines like [[Haru, Hidden Talent]] and [[Sanctum of Calm Waters]] to keep generating counters and cards.

keep.text: [[Sol Ring]] into a cheap engine piece like [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] starts the plan.
Early ramp backed by a way to draw more cards keeps the hand moving.

sendBack.text: A hand missing colors to cast its bending spells struggles across five colors.
A hand with no early plays to reach the commander around turn 4 falls behind.

tips.text: [[Iroh, Dragon of the West]] gives firebending to creatures with counters, pairing with [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]]'s earthbend triggers.
[[Wan Shi Tong, Librarian]] punishes opponents' tutors, drawing cards whenever they search their library.
[[Guru Pathik]] finds Lesson, Saga, or Shrine cards to fuel [[Gran-Gran]]'s loot ability and the graveyard count.

reply.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color deck built around the four bending triggers, Lesson spells, and Shrine payoffs, drawing cards off waterbend, earthbend, firebend, and airbend effects to flip into Aang, Master of Elements and eventually transform again for life, draws, counters and damage. The deck can also assemble infinite creature ETB and LTB loops using [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] alongside [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander.

strategy.text: Ramp early with mana rocks and land tutors to reach [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Trigger all four bending types to draw cards and transform into [[Aang, Master of Elements]].
Chain Lesson spells to fuel [[Gran-Gran]], [[Uncle Iroh]], and [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] discounts and counters.
Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander for infinite ETB loops.
Use Shrine enchantments to snowball lands, tokens and card draw as the game goes long.

keep.text: [[Sol Ring]] alongside an early bending spell sets up the whole plan fast.
[[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] plus a cheap airbend piece supports the combo line.

sendBack.text: A hand without fixing for five colors struggles to cast Lesson spells on time.
Too few lands relative to spells leaves bending triggers stranded in hand.

tips.text: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] airbends a permanent, and [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] turns casting it from exile into a token.
[[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] draws a card whenever you airbend, so [[Monk Gyatso]] exiling a targeted creature triggers it too.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbends off any spell, and Lesson spells add an extra counter to that land.

rendered.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifacts deck built around counters: every time Kilo taps, it proliferates, pushing +1/+1, charge, and other counters across the board. The deck layers proliferate payoffs like [[Contagion Engine]], [[Tezzeret's Gambit]], and [[Astral Cornucopia]] to grow value, and assembles combos such as [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana, or [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns.

strategy: Cast ramp artifacts early like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to accelerate toward [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]].
Deploy [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3 and tap it repeatedly to trigger proliferate.
Use proliferate engines such as [[Contagion Engine]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] to multiply counters each turn.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana to fuel the board.
Chain [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns to close the game.

Too few artifacts to proliferate leaves [[Contagion Clasp]] stranded.

Use [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] with [[Pemmin's Aura]] and [[Relic of Legends]] to proliferate without limit.

repairReply.overview: [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] leads a colorless ramp deck that reaches seven mana to cast huge spells like [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] and [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] which then cascade twice into more threats. Artifacts such as [[Sol Ring]] and [[Thran Dynamo]] accelerate the plan, while [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana as a finishing line. strategy: Ramp early with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]].
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to put Dinosaurs like [[Polyraptor]] directly onto the battlefield.
Trigger Enrage on [[Polyraptor]] or [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] with fight or damage effects to build loops.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] for infinite tokens and damage to all creatures.
Close games with wide Dinosaur boards buffed by [[Garruk's Uprising]] or [[Rite of Passage]].

keep: [[Walking Ballista]] alongside early ramp sets up a quick board presence.
A hand with [[Forerunner of the Empire]] can find Dinosaurs to build toward value.
sendBack: A hand lacking any green or red source struggles to cast the Naya curve.

[[Forerunner of the Empire]] damages creatures whenever a Dinosaur enters, synergizing with tokens from [[Polyraptor]].

[[Rite of Passage]] grows creatures damaged by [[Forerunner of the Empire]] or combat with [[Polyraptor]].

repairReply.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a Dimir ninjutsu deck that slips unblockable creatures through, swaps them for Ninjas like [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Fallen Shinobi]], and wins by piling up combat damage triggers off [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] herself, draining life equal to each revealed card's mana value while refilling the hand.

strategy.text: Deploy early evasive creatures such as [[Tormented Soul]] and [[Slither Blade]] to set up ninjutsu returns.
Return an unblocked attacker to hand and ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] for value.
Trigger combat damage with Ninjas to reveal cards off [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]], draining life and drawing cards.
Use [[Fallen Shinobi]] and [[Higure, the Still Wind]] to generate extra resources and find more Ninjas.
Ramp with [[Sol Ring]] and [[Dimir Signet]] to cast [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] around turn 3 and keep the chain going.

keep.text: [[Tormented Soul]] into [[Mistblade Shinobi]] starts turns early.
[[Prosperous Thief]] ready to attack sets up Treasures early.

sendBack.text: A hand without blue mana can't cast [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] on time.
Without a card like [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] to start the attack, ninjutsu stalls.

tips.text: [[Satoru Umezawa]] turns any creature in hand into a cheap ninjutsu threat alongside [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].
[[Fallen Shinobi]] lets you cast cards exiled from an opponent's library, pairing well with [[Nashi, Moon Sage's Scion]]'s similar trigger.
[[Moon-Circuit Hacker]] draws a card on hit, refueling the hand for more ninjutsu swaps with [[Mistblade Shinobi]].

[[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] turns every point of combat damage into card advantage and direct life loss equal to the revealed card's mana value, closing games through repeated small attacks rather than big swings.

Chain extra Ninja triggers with [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Fallen Shinobi]] for reanimation and card advantage.
Protect the attack step with counterspells like [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] to keep combat damage flowing.
